59473-the-story-of-dutch-painting.title: Dutch Painting
59473-the-story-of-dutch-painting.creator: Unknown
59473-the-story-of-dutch-painting.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. On the 25th of October, 1555, Charles V abdicated the imperial crown, ceding Spain and the Netherlands to his favorite son, Philip II. The event proved to be the prologue of a drama, which in its immediate aspects involved the decay of Spain and the growth of Holland, but in its wider significance was to be the beginning of a new era.

arxiv-2102-00324.title: Video Reenactment as Inductive Bias for Content-Motion Disentanglement
arxiv-2102-00324.creator: J. F. Hernández Albarracín, A. Ramírez Rivera
arxiv-2102-00324.description: Abstract Independent components within low-dimensional representations are essential inputs in several downstream tasks, and provide explanations over the observed data. Video-based disentangled factors of variation provide low-dimensional representations that can be identified and used to feed task-specific models. We introduce MTC-VAE, a self-supervised motion-transfer VAE model to disentangle motion and content from videos.

arxiv-2102-13351.title: Engineering Swarms of Cyber-Physical Systems with the CPSwarm Workbench
arxiv-2102-13351.creator: Micha Sende, Melanie Schranz, Gianluca Prato, Etienne Brosse, Omar Morando, Martina Umlauft
arxiv-2102-13351.description: Abstract Engineering swarms of cyber-physical systems (CPSs) is a complex process. We present the CPSwarm workbench that creates an automated design workflow to ease this process. This formalized workflow guides the user from modeling, to code generation, to deployment, both in simulation and on CPS hardware platforms. The workbench combines existing and emerging tools to solve real-world CPS swarm problems.

arxiv-2203-02917.title: Intertwining of Complementary Thue-Morse Factors
arxiv-2203-02917.creator: Jeffrey Shallit
arxiv-2203-02917.description: Abstract We consider the positions of occurrences of a factor x x and its binary complement x ¯ \overline{x} in the Thue-Morse word 𝐭 = 𝟶𝟷𝟷𝟶𝟷𝟶𝟶𝟷 ⋯ {\bf t}={\tt 01101001}\cdots , and show that these occurrences are “intertwined” in essentially two different ways.

arxiv-2204-11334.title: Hardware Acceleration for Third-Generation FHE and PSI Based on It
arxiv-2204-11334.creator: Zhehong Wang, Dennis Sylvester, Hun-Seok Kim, David Blaauw
arxiv-2204-11334.description: Abstract With the expansion of cloud services, serious concerns about the privacy of users’ data arise due to the exposure of the unencrypted data to the server during computation. Various security primitives are under investigation to preserve privacy while evaluating private data, including Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), Private Set Intersection (PSI), and others.

arxiv-2205-09693.title: Individual and Collective Performance Deteriorate in a New Team: A Case Study of CS:GO Tournaments
arxiv-2205-09693.creator: Weiwei Zhang, Goran Muric ID, Emilio Ferrara ID
arxiv-2205-09693.description: Abstract How does the team formation relates to team performance in professional video game playing? This study examined one aspect of group dynamics - team switching - and aims to answer how changing a team affects individual and collective performance in eSports tournaments.

arxiv-2206-12522.title: Possible Universal Limit for Valence Parton Distributions
arxiv-2206-12522.creator: Christopher Leon, Misak M. Sargsian
arxiv-2206-12522.description: Abstract We report the observation of the existence of a possible universal limit for valence parton distributions that should exist once partonic degrees of freedom are relevant for high energy scattering from strongly interacting bound systems like a nucleon, meson or a few nucleon system at very short distances.

arxiv-2305-12915.title: What do the fast dynamics tell us about aggregation?
arxiv-2305-12915.creator: Tamoghna Das
arxiv-2305-12915.description: Abstract Two typical morphology of two-dimensional aggregates are considered: compact crystalline clusters and string-like non-compact conformations. Simulated trajectories of both types of aggregates are analysed with fine spatial resolution. While the long-time geometry of such trajectories appears to be statistically identical for two conformations, the self-overlap statistics reveal two distinct short-time pre-caging mechanisms.

arxiv-2308-15506.title: Accurate determination of excitation energy: An equation-of-motion approach over a bi-exponential Coupled Cluster theory
arxiv-2308-15506.creator: Anish Chakraborty, Pradipta Kumar Samanta, Rahul Maitra
arxiv-2308-15506.description: Abstract The calculation of molecular excited states is critically important to decipher a plethora of molecular properties. In this manuscript, we develop an equation of motion formalism on top of a bi-exponentially parametrized ground state wavefunction towards the determination of excited states.

arxiv-2601-16525.title: Bosonization Solution to Spin-Valley Kondo Problem: Finite-Size Spectrum and Renormalization Group Analysis
arxiv-2601-16525.creator: Yi-Jie Wang, Geng-Dong Zhou, Hyunsung Jung, Seongyeon Youn, Seung-Sup B. Lee, Zhi-Da Song
arxiv-2601-16525.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yi-Jie Wang, Geng-Dong Zhou, Hyunsung Jung, Seongyeon Youn, Seung-Sup B. Lee, Zhi-Da Song. Spin-valley Anderson impurities (SVAIM) with (anti-)Hund’s splitting provide a natural explanation to the origin of pairing potential and pseudogap in the magic-angle graphene Wang et al. In this work, we derive and analytically solve the low-energy Kondo theories for SVAIM at half-filling, with especial focus on the two anti-Hund’s regimes: the impurity is either dominated by a valley doublet, or a trivial singlet.

plos-pone-0000158.description: PLOS ONE research article. Evolutionary History of LINE-1 in the Major Clades of Placental Mammals

pmc-10531401.title: Ion fluxes Involved in the Adaptation of the Estuarine Diatom Coscinodiscus centralis Ehrenberg to Salinity Stress
pmc-10531401.creator: Changping Chen, Xiao Hu, Yahui Gao, Junrong Liang, Lin Sun, Elena R Tarakhovskaya
pmc-10531401.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Although estuarine diatoms have a wide range of salt tolerance, they are often severely stressed by elevated salt concentrations. It remains poorly understood how estuarine diatoms maintain ionic homeostasis under high-salinity conditions. Using a scanning ion-selective electrode technique, this study determined the fluxes of H+, Na+, and K+ involved in the acclimatization of the estuarine diatom Coscinodiscus centralis Ehrenberg after an elevation in salinity from 15 psu to 35 psu.

pmc-10716772.title: A comparison of treatment response to biologics in asthma-COPD overlap and pure asthma: Findings from the PRISM study
pmc-10716772.creator: Ji-Su Shim, Hyunkyoung Kim, Jae-Woo Kwon, So-Young Park, Sujeong Kim, Byung-Keun Kim, Young-Hee Nam, Min-Suk Yang, Mi-Yeong Kim, Sae-Hoon Kim, Byung-Jae Lee, Taehoon Lee, Sang-Ha Kim, So Young Park, Young-Joo Cho, Chan Sun Park, Jae-Woo Jung, Han-Ki Park, Joo-Hee Kim, Jeong-Hee Choi, Ji-Yong Moon, I
pmc-10716772.description: BackgroundDespite the increasing use of biologics in severe asthma, there is limited research on their use in asthma-chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap (ACO). We compared real-world treatment responses to biologics in ACO and asthma.MethodsWe conducted a multicenter, retrospective, cohort study using data from the Precision Medicine Intervention in Severe Asthma (PRISM).

pmc-11389368.title: An intracellular phosphorus-starvation signal activates the PhoB/PhoR two-component system in Salmonella enterica
pmc-11389368.creator: Roberto E. Bruna, Christopher G. Kendra, Mauricio H. Pontes
pmc-11389368.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bacteria acquire P primarily as inorganic orthophosphate (Pi, PO43−). Once internalized, Pi is rapidly assimilated into biomass during the synthesis of ATP. Because Pi is essential, but excessive ATP is toxic, the acquisition of environmental Pi is tightly regulated. In the bacterium Salmonella enterica (Salmonella), growth in Pi-limiting environments activates the membrane sensor histidine kinase PhoR, leading to the phosphorylation of its cognate transcriptional regulator PhoB and subsequent transcription of genes involved in adaptations to low Pi.

pmc-11507544.title: Descriptive Representation and Reproductive Health Outcomes: The Role of Women Candidates in Reducing Teen Birth Rates
pmc-11507544.creator: Jeronimo Cortina, Shana Hardin
pmc-11507544.description: Background/Objectives: Teen birth rates remain a pressing public health issue in the United States, with significant long-term health risks for both mothers and children. Previous research has primarily focused on the impact of women in elected office on reproductive health outcomes, but less is known about the influence of women candidates.

pmc-11510566.title: Protective Effects of Sesame Glycoproteins on Ultraviolet-Induced Skin Aging: In Vitro and In Vivo Studies
pmc-11510566.creator: Kyung Kyu Baik, Woo-Yong Song, Dong Keun Song, Jaehyeok Yun, Ji Hwan Jang, Jae Young Oh, Mi-Jin Lee, Eunjandi Go, Kyong Jin Lee, Eunmiri Roh, Jong-Eun Kim
pmc-11510566.description: Background/Objectives: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation is a primary factor in skin photoaging, leading to wrinkles, reduced elasticity, and pigmentation changes due to damage to cellular DNA, proteins, and lipids. Glycoproteins from sesame cake (SPE) have potential protective effects against UV-induced skin aging.

pmc-11652561.title: Profiling immune cell-related gene features and immunoregulatory ceRNA in ischemic stroke
pmc-11652561.creator: Yanbo Li, Sicheng Liu, Linda Wen, Linzhu Zhang, Xue Lei, Yaguang Zhang, Lei Qiu, Li He, Junhong Han
pmc-11652561.description: Molecules in immune cells plays a vital role in the pathogenesis of ischemic stroke (IS). The aim of this study is to profile the landscape of molecules on the basis of immune cells in IS peripheral blood and construct an immunoregulatory competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network.

pmc-12455169.title: Enhancing Team-Based Learning in Medical Education: Integration of Multidisciplinary Scenarios and Objective Structured Practical Examination (OSPE) in a Retrospective Study at the College of Medicine, Qassim University, Saudi Arabia
pmc-12455169.creator: Mostafa M Khodeir, Homaidan Alhomaidan, Ali Shariq, Elsayed A Elmorsy
pmc-12455169.description: BackgroundTraditional team-based learning (TBL) in medical education often lacks multidisciplinary integration and practical skills assessment, typically relying on multiple-choice questions without clinical competency evaluation.ObjectiveTo evaluate our re-engineered (redesigned), multidisciplinary TBL model, incorporating objective structured practical examination (OSPE) assessments, and its impact on student engagement, performance, and gender achievement gaps.

pmc-12551236.title: Echoes from Macondo: managing disseminated ascariasis with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation therapy. A case report
pmc-12551236.creator: Andres Felipe Herazo-Cubillos, Daniela Umaña-Gómez, Juan Sebastian Montoya-Beltran, Laura Ramirez-Herrrera, Andres Duque-Estevez, Carlos Miguel Santacruz-Escudero
pmc-12551236.description: Ascaris lumbricoides is one of the most prevalent helminthic infections worldwide, yet disseminated disease is rare. In resource-limited settings, delayed diagnosis can lead to severe complications, including multiorgan dysfunction and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). There are only sporadic case reports describing the management of this entity with mechanical circulatory support such as extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO).

pmc-13451717.title: Prevalence, associated factors, and antibiotic susceptibility of bacterial isolates in suspected ear infections at University of Gondar Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia: A cross-sectional study
pmc-13451717.creator: Anmut Amare, Mitkie Tigabie, Getnet Ayalew, Wondwossen Abebe, Yitayih Wondimeneh
pmc-13451717.description: BackgroundEar infections affect millions worldwide, causing significant hearing loss, particularly in developing countries. Bacterial infections play a major role, necessitating studies on causative agents, risk factors, and antibiotic resistance.ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the prevalence, associated factors, and antibiotic susceptibility of the bacterial isolates among patients in suspected ear infections at the University of Gondar Hospital, Ethiopia.

pmc-13538188.title: Integrated Study of Polyethylene Microplastic Degradation and Its Interaction with the Insecticide Imidacloprid: Chronic Toxicity to Daphnia similis
pmc-13538188.creator: Maria Eduarda Kiihl, Thandy Junio da Silva Pinto, Mariana Amaral Dias, Cassiana Carolina Montagner, Evaldo Luiz Gaeta Espíndola, David Silva Alexandre
pmc-13538188.description: The presence of microplastics (MPs) in freshwater environments represents a growing environmental concern due to their persistence and ability to interact with contaminants such as pesticides. This study evaluated the influence of photodegradation on the toxicity of polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs), alone and combined with the pesticide Imidacloprid (IMI), on the cladoceran Daphnia similis.

pmc-13622911.title: Shaping the Flow: Impact of Blade Shape on Performance and Hemocompatibility in Rotodynamic Blood Pumps
pmc-13622911.creator: Benjamin Torner, Simon Klocker, Niccolò Crescenti, Aldo J. Suria, Harald Reithofer, Michael Hübler, Daniel Zimpfer, Marcus Granegger
pmc-13622911.description: ObjectivesRotodynamic blood pumps (RBPs) must operate reliably across a wide range of clinical conditions, including off‐design operating regimes. Although blade shape is known to influence off‐design performance in conventional turbopumps, its impact on hydraulic performance and hemocompatibility in RBPs has not been systematically investigated.

pmc-13679924.title: Nanoscale Buried Interface Control in Silicone Hydrogels Enables a Biointerface Engineering Platform
pmc-13679924.creator: Po‐Hsiang Chen, Jia‐Hua Wang, Ching Chen, Shih‐Hsuan Fu, Rajan Deepan Chakravarthy, Hsin‐Chieh Lin
pmc-13679924.description: Engineering multifunctional biointerfaces requires quantitative understanding of how buried nanoscale coating architectures govern biological function, yet such relationships remain inaccessible because non‐destructive characterization of soft, curved interfaces is lacking. Here, we establish an integrated engineering–characterization–function platform that quantitatively resolves buried nanocoatings and directly correlates their architecture with interfacial performance.
